rules.title: Application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: An application screening fee may not exceed the actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information about the applicant, and in no case more than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The landlord may adjust the $30 amount annually in line with increases in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.key_value: Actual out-of-pocket costs, not to exceed $30 per applicant, adjustable annually commensurate with the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who charge applicants, including guarantors or cosignors, a fee to screen a request to rent a residential property.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property or their agents charging application screening fees.
rules.quoted_span: (1) A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: Required screening process and refunds as condition for charging fee
rules.requirement: A screening fee may be charged only if the landlord offers either a first-come screening process (applications considered in order received, written screening criteria provided, first qualifying applicant approved, no fee charged until the application is actually considered, with any inadvertently collected fee refunded within seven days) or a process returning the entire fee to every applicant not selected within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days of submission, whichever occurs first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selecting an applicant or 30 days of submission, whichever occurs first (option B); refund of inadvertently collected fees within seven days (option A)
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property or their agents collecting application screening fees.
rules.exemptions: Under the first-come process, a landlord need not refund the fee to an applicant whose application is denied after consideration for not meeting the landlord's established screening criteria; the landlord may offer to apply the fee to another rental unit instead of refunding.
rules.quoted_span: (2) A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:

rules.title: Itemized receipt and return of unused fee
rules.requirement: The landlord must give the applicant a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing information about the applicant, delivered personally, by mail, or by email if agreed. If no personal reference check or credit report is obtained, any unused portion of the fee must be returned.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property or their agents who collect an application screening fee.
rules.quoted_span: (d) The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.

rules.title: Copy of consumer credit report to applicant
rules.requirement: If an applicant paid a screening fee, the landlord must provide the applicant a copy of their consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving it.
rules.key_value: Within seven days of receiving the report
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential rental property or their agents who collected an application screening fee and obtained a consumer credit report.
rules.quoted_span: (f) If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
